main_text.l: 4 An omne ens quatenus ens habeat existentiam?
Statuitur thesis affirmatiua. Rationes sunt: 1, Quia
existentia est proprietas cuiusque entis quatenus ens
est. Ideoque a nullo ente abesse potest. 2, Quia actus &
infeparabilis nexus est inter existentiam & essentiam,
ita ut nulli enti possit vere attribui essentia, quin etiam
necesse sit attribui existentiam. Siquidem existentia im-
mediate fluit ab essentia entis tanquam effectum a sua
proxima causa efficiente. 3, Quia destructa existentia
destruitur ipsa essentia, & ex cōsequenti ipsum ens. Hinc
recte Fr. Suarez disput. 31. sect. 12. context. 1. asserit, im-
possibile esse ita separari existentiam ab essentia, ut con-
servetur existentia destructa essentia. Item context. 5.

page.notes: Hyphenated words at line ends are kept as printed. Uncertain readings: "reftatur" (Zabarella passage) and the marginal word "[?]azatur" (the left-margin verb after "Error quorundam Scholast.", probably "notatur"; not clear enough to read). The last word of the page, "qu[?]run-", is unclear; the line ends with a printed hyphen. The placement of the roman numerals I., II., III. in the left margin is approximate, judged from their line position. The Suárez references are set in italics as they appear to be printed. The heading "4 An omne ens..." is treated as a numbered question heading (level 2). The large initial "S" of "Statuitur" is joined to the word. Printed "Item context. 5." and "cōsequenti" are copied as read.
